title: Impact of Rising Inflation on Planned GST Increase and Related Financial Offset Measures
what_it_is: Impact of Rising Inflation on Planned GST Increase and Related Financial Offset Measures

sections.label: Questions on $1.5 billion support package
sections.summary: MPs asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance about the tracking indicators, considerations, thresholds and risks behind the $1.5 billion support package.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) what tracking indicators have been used to determine the latest $1.5 billion support package to help Singaporeans cope with inflation; and (b) whether the Government will consider temporarily enhancing the GST offset package for the lower- and middle-income groups if inflationary pressures continue unabated with the impending GST hikes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) what are the key considerations in the sizing and distribution of the latest $1.5 billion support package; (b) whether the various cost pressures faced by different segments of Singaporeans can be further mitigated; and (c) whether the Government will have the fiscal space to introduce further assistance measures in this financial year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether the $1.5 billion support package announced recently and the Assurance Package will continue to offset the five to 10 years of additional GST expenses for Singaporean households; (b) what are the quantitative or qualitative thresholds that will trigger another support package; (c) whether there are any updates on non-fiscal and exchange rate policy measures to address rising prices driven by supply side factors; and (d) what are the risks of a wage-price spiral emerging in Singapore over the next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance what are the considerations in determining the size, scope and duration of the support measures in the $1.5 billion support package, including the assumptions on inflation beyond September 2022.

sections.label: MAS S$NEER band tightening
sections.summary: MAS raised the appreciation path of the Singapore dollar nominal effective exchange rate policy band three times in the past nine months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: MAS has raised the appreciation path of the Singapore dollar nominal effective exchange rate (S$NEER) policy band three times in the past nine months – in October last year, in January and in April this year.

sections.label: Announcement of $1.5 billion package
sections.summary: A $1.5 billion support package was announced last month in response to the more challenging global inflation environment, especially sharp increases in energy and food prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Last month, I announced a $1.5 billion support package, in response to the more challenging global inflation environment in recent months, especially the sharp increases in energy and food prices.

sections.label: GST Vouchers and utility rebates
sections.summary: About 1.5 million lower- to middle-income Singaporeans will receive GST Voucher Cash and Special Payment of up to $700 in August, and HDB households will receive utility bill rebates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, after putting together all the measures, about 1.5 million lower- to middle-income Singaporeans, including retirees, will receive a GST Voucher – Cash and Special Payment of up to $700 in August this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Households living in 4-room HDB flats will receive a total of about five months' worth of rebates on their utility bills for the whole of Financial Year of 2022, while those in 3-room flats will receive about seven months' worth of rebates.

sections.label: Enhanced Progressive Wage Credit Scheme co-funding
sections.summary: Under the $1.5 billion support package, the Government enhanced its co-funding share under the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme to pay up to 75% of lower-wage workers' wage increases this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, as part of the $1.5 billion support package, I had enhanced the Government's co-funding share for this year under the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This means that the Government will pay up to 75% of the wage increase of our lower-wage workers this year.

sections.label: GST increase and Assurance Package
sections.summary: The Government will proceed with the staggered GST increase, set aside a $6.6 billion Assurance Package, and not push back the increase further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And this is why the Government will need to go ahead with the GST increase as announced at Budget 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We had already anticipated the higher inflation outlook earlier this year and that is why, instead of a two-percentage point increase this year, I had decided to delay and stagger the GST increase over two steps – by one-percentage point from January 2023, and another one-percentage point from January 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We should not push back the GST increase any further, as we will need the funds urgently to take better care of our growing number of seniors and to meet our rising healthcare expenditures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That said, we have already set aside the $6.6 billion Assurance Package to cushion all Singaporean households from the impact of the GST increase.

sections.label: GST increase commitment review
sections.summary: The Government updated its inflation outlook and will review the situation, enhancing the Assurance Package if needed to uphold its commitments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First, as I have said in my reply, we have done an update based on the latest inflation outlook.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are still able to assure today that our commitment holds, that the majority of Singaporean households will not feel the impact of the GST increase for five years and for the lower-income households, it will be 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Inflation can be much higher than we had expected and for longer durations too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we will continue to review the situation, and as I mentioned in my reply, if the need arises, we will enhance the Assurance Package to uphold our commitments.

sections.label: GST increase and funding gap
sections.summary: Without the GST increase, Singapore risks a persistent structural funding gap that widens yearly, with the figure expected to reach 20% of GDP by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: By 2030, we expect this to rise to 20% of GDP, or maybe even more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, the short answer to the question, what will happen if we do not have this GST increase, is simple.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will be at risk of a persistent structural funding gap, which will continue to widen year by year.

sections.label: Funding $1.5 billion package
sections.summary: Revenue upside and Omicron spending savings let the Government mount a $1.5 billion package within its current budget, targeting lower-income and vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we did enjoy this upside this year and on the expenditure side, it so turned out, fortunately, for us that Omicron was milder than we had expected and so we had some savings on the spending side.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And that was exactly why – because of both the revenue and expenditure savings – we were able to mount this recent $1.5 billion package within our current budget, within our current means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the second point, we had designed the $1.5 billion package precisely to help lower-income households, families, workers, as well as the more vulnerable groups.

sections.label: Package and Budget measures ahead
sections.summary: Package and Budget measures will still be implemented in coming months, including cash payouts up to $700 in August, utilities rebates and CDC vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The measures in this package, as well as the measures that were announced in the Budget will still be implemented in the months ahead, including the additional cash payout which I mentioned just now, up to $700 in August, the utilities rebates, CDC vouchers coming up soon.

sections.label: Question on household expenditure impact
sections.summary: The question asks the Government to share its assessment of higher household expenditures from inflation and the offset from the $1.5 billion package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Would the Government be able to share with us the assessment of the increase in household expenditures as a result of the higher inflation expectations and what is the expected offset in household expenditures as a result of this $1.5 billion package?

sections.label: Targeting lower-income households
sections.summary: Higher-than-expected inflation impacts households, so the package targets lower-income and vulnerable groups who bear the greater brunt of higher prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Obviously, with the higher-than- expected inflation, there will be an impact on households and that is precisely why we had put in place this package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we have, as I mentioned in my reply, been very careful to target the measures more for the lower-income and vulnerable groups, because they are the ones who will bear the greater brunt of higher prices.
